rules.title: Acronyms
rules.rule: Don’t use periods for acronyms. Examples: FIAT; LGBT.

options.label: Don’t use spaces
options.rule: When writing uppercase acronyms, don’t use spaces. Examples: FIAT; LGBT.

options.label: Use spaces
options.rule: When writing uppercase acronyms, use spaces. Examples: F I A T; L G B T.

options.label: Write them in words
options.rule: When writing centuries, write them in words. Examples: Il ventesimo secolo; il Novecento.

options.label: Write them in numerals
options.rule: When writing centuries, write them in numerals. Examples: Il XX secolo; il ’900.

options.label: Use hyphens
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use hyphens. Example: 22-09-1996.

options.label: Use periods
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use periods. Example: 22.09.1996.

options.label: Use slashes
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use slashes. Example: 22/09/1996.

options.label: Write them in words
options.rule: When writing decades, write them in words. Example: Gli anni Sessanta.

options.label: Write them in figures with the apostrophe
options.rule: When writing decades, write them in figures, abbreviated, and with the apostrophe. Example: Gli anni ’60.

options.label: Write them in figures without the apostrophe
options.rule: When writing decades, write them in figures, abbreviated, and without the apostrophe. Example: Gli anni 60.

options.label: Don’t use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit days and months, don’t use a leading zero. Example: 4/3/95.

options.label: Use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit days and months, use a leading zero. Example: 04/03/95.

rules.title: Writing dates
rules.rule: Write dates with days and years in figures and months in letters. Example: 22 settembre 1996.

options.label: Write only the last two figures preceded by an apostrophe
options.rule: When writing years, write only the last two figures preceded by an apostrophe. Example: ’89.

options.label: Write the year in full
options.rule: When writing years, write the year in full. Example: 1989.

options.label: Use a colon
options.rule: To separate hours, minutes, and seconds, use a colon. Example: 18:45:37.

options.label: Use a period
options.rule: To separate hours, minutes, and seconds, use a period. Example: 18.45.37.

options.label: Use 00:00
options.rule: When indicating midnight in numerals, use 00:00.

options.label: Use 24:00
options.rule: When indicating midnight in numerals, use 24:00.

options.label: Don’t use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit hours, don’t use a leading zero. Example: 5:50.

options.label: Use a leading zero
options.rule: For single-digit hours, use a leading zero. Example: 05:50.

options.label: Use the currency symbol after the amount, without a space
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the currency symbol after the amount, without a space. Example: 5€.

options.label: Use the currency symbol after the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the currency symbol after the amount, with a space. Example: 5 €.

options.label: Use the ISO code after the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the ISO code after the amount, with a space. Example: 5 EUR.

options.label: Spell out the word after the amount and in lowercase
options.rule: When writing currencies, spell out the word after the amount and in lowercase. Example: 5 euro.

options.label: Use the currency symbol before the amount, without a space
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the currency symbol before the amount, without a space. Example: €5.

options.label: Use the currency symbol before the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing currencies, use the currency symbol before the amount, with a space. Example: € 5.

options.label: Spell out “milione” and “miliardo”
options.rule: When writing large sums of money, spell out the words “milione” and “miliardo”. Examples: 8 milioni; 15 miliardi.

options.label: Use “mio” and “mrd”
options.rule: When writing large sums of money, use “mio” and “mrd” instead of “milione” and “miliardo”. Examples: 8 mio; 15 mrd.

options.label: Use % without a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use % without a space. Example: 99%.

options.label: Write “per cento”
options.rule: When writing percentages, write “per cento”. Example: 99 per cento.

options.label: Write “percento”
options.rule: When writing percentages, write “percento”. Example: 99 percento.

options.label: Use % with a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, use % with a space. Example: 99 %.

options.label: Abbreviate with a numeral but spell out without
examples: Ha percorso diversi chilometri a piedi
options.rule: For units of measure, abbreviate when used with a numeral but spell out when used without. Examples: 12 kg; Ha percorso diversi chilometri a piedi.

options.label: Always abbreviate
examples: Ha percorso diversi km a piedi
options.rule: For units of measure, always abbreviate, with or without a numeral. Example: Ha percorso diversi km a piedi.

options.label: Always spell out
options.rule: For units of measure, always spell out, with or without a numeral. Example: Ha percorso 10 chilometri a piedi.

options.label: Spell out units with spelled-out numbers, abbreviate with numerals
options.rule: When numbers are spelled out, spell out the units; when numbers are written as numerals, abbreviate the units. Examples: Pesa due chili; Pesa 12 kg.

options.label: Don’t use a space between a numeral and unit
options.rule: For units of measure, don’t use a space between a numeral and unit. Example: 12kg.

options.label: Use a space between a numeral and unit
options.rule: For units of measure, use a space between a numeral and unit. Example: 12 kg.

options.label: Write the name of the unit of measure in full
options.rule: When writing temperatures, write the name of the unit of measure in full. Examples: 32 gradi Celsius; 98 gradi Fahrenheit; 37 gradi Kelvin.

options.label: Use “grado” or “gradi” without specifying the scale
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use the word “grado” or “gradi” without specifying the temperature scale. Examples: Cinque gradi; 25 gradi.

options.label: Use numerals followed by the unit symbol, with a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals followed by the unit symbol, with a space. Examples: 32 °C; 98 °F; 37 K.

options.label: Use numerals followed by the unit symbol, without a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use numerals followed by the unit symbol, without a space. Examples: 32°C; 98°F; 37K.

options.label: Use a period as the thousands separator
options.rule: For thousands separators, use a period as the thousands separator. Example: 25.000.

options.label: Use a space as the thousands separator
options.rule: For thousands separators, use a space as the thousands separator. Example: 25 000.

options.label: Don’t use spaces
options.rule: When writing phone numbers, don’t use spaces. Example: +3912345678.

options.label: Use a space after the country code
options.rule: When writing phone numbers, use a space after the country code. Example: +39 12345678.

rules.title: When indicating a range of numbers or dates

options.label: Use a hyphen with spaces
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use a hyphen (-) with spaces. Examples: 2001 - 2003; lunedì - venerdì.

options.label: Use a hyphen without spaces
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use a hyphen (-) without spaces. Examples: 2001-2003; lunedì-venerdì.

options.label: Use “da…a”
options.rule: When indicating a range of numbers or dates, use “da…a” (“from...to”). Examples: Dal 2001 al 2003; dal lunedì al venerdì.

options.label: Use curly quotation marks and the curly apostrophe
options.rule: Use double (“...”) and single (‘...’) curly quotation marks and the curly apostrophe (’). Example: “Sarà per un’altra volta!”.

options.label: Use straight quotation marks and the straight apostrophe
options.rule: Use double ("...") and single ('...') straight quotation marks and the straight apostrophe ('). Example: "Sarà per un'altra volta!".

options.label: Use guillemets and the curly apostrophe
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») and the curly apostrophe (’). Example: «Sarà per un’altra volta!».

options.label: Use guillemets and the straight apostrophe
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») and the straight apostrophe ('). Example: «Sarà per un'altra volta!».

options.label: Use curly double marks and curly single marks inside
options.rule: Use double curly quotation marks (“...”) for quotes and single ones (‘...’) for quotes within quotes. Example: “Preferiamo un approccio ‘human-in-the-loop’”.

options.label: Use straight double marks and straight single marks inside
options.rule: Use double straight quotation marks ("...") for quotes and single ones ('...') for quotes within quotes. Example: "Preferiamo un approccio 'human-in-the-loop'".

options.label: Use guillemets and curly double marks inside
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») for quotes and double curly quotation marks (“...”) for quotes within quotes. Example: «Preferiamo un approccio “human-in-the-loop”».

options.label: Use guillemets and straight double marks inside
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») for quotes and double straight quotation marks ("...") for quotes within quotes. Example: «Preferiamo un approccio "human-in-the-loop"».

options.label: Use guillemets and single guillemets inside
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») for quotes and single guillemets (‹...›) for quotes within quotes. Example: «Preferiamo un approccio ‹human-in-the-loop›».

rules.title: Passive voice
rules.rule: Use active voice. Use passive voice only when the agent is unknown or irrelevant.

rules.title: Capitalization
examples: CISL, UIL e UGL sono tre confederazioni sindacali italiane
rules.rule: Don’t use all caps, except when writing out an acronym, initialism, or proper noun. Example: CISL, UIL e UGL sono tre confederazioni sindacali italiane.

options.label: Don’t make changes to quoted material
options.rule: When including quotes, don’t make changes to quoted material, regardless of style rules.

options.label: Edit quoted material to adhere to style rules
options.rule: When including quotes, edit quoted material to adhere to style rules.

options.label: Use the formal “lei”
options.rule: When addressing the reader, use the formal “lei”.

options.label: Use the informal “tu”
options.rule: When addressing the reader, use the informal “tu”.

rules.title: Inclusive language
rules.rule: Replace binary representations of gender with gender-neutral language.

rules.title: When gender is not specified and when referring to a group with people of mixed genders

options.label: Use both the feminine and the masculine forms
examples: Gli alunni e le alunne sono rientrati
options.rule: When gender is not specified and when referring to a group with people of mixed genders, use both the feminine and the masculine forms. Example: Gli alunni e le alunne sono rientrati.

options.label: Use universal feminine form
options.rule: When gender is not specified and when referring to a group with people of mixed genders, use universal feminine form (“femminile sovraesteso”). Examples: Ho visto qualcuna passare; Le alunne sono rientrate.

options.label: Use inclusive nouns and adjectives
options.rule: When gender is not specified and when referring to a group with people of mixed genders, use inclusive nouns and adjectives. Examples: Ho visto una persona passare; La classe è rientrata.

options.label: Use universal masculine form
options.rule: When gender is not specified and when referring to a group with people of mixed genders, use universal masculine form (“maschile sovraesteso”). Examples: Ho visto qualcuno passare; Gli alunni sono rientrati.

rules.title: When referring to non-binary people
rules.rule: When referring to non-binary people, use the schwa (“ə”) ending for singular forms and the plural schwa (“ɜ”) ending for plural forms. The pronouns are “ləi” for the singular form and “loro” for the plural form. Examples: Ləi è laureatə; Loro sono laureatɜ; Ti presento lə miə amicə; Loro sono lɜ miɜ amicɜ.
